Ministry of Justice
First and Second District Courts
post of
MAGISTRATE 1
Qualifications:
Applicants should possess:
LLM Degree plus a Certificate in Legal 
Education and a minimum of three (3) 
years legal experience;
or
Bachelor of Law Degree plus a Certificate 
in Legal Education and a minimum of four 
(4) years legal experience.
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be required 
to:
Preside over and determine Criminal, 
Quasi-Criminal and Civil Matters and 
Preliminary matters in the First and 
Second Judicial Districts Courts of 
St. Lucia;
Act as Coroner and preside at inquests;
Perform all such other duties that may be 
so performed by a Magistrate.
Salary and Allowance:
Salary is in the range of $54,508.11 - 
$56,399.75 per annum (Grade 17)
Legal Officer’s allowance - 
$1,500.00 per month
Travelling allowance -
 $464.00 per month
Telephone allowance - 
$24.25 per month

of documents pertaining to qualifications 
should be addressed to:
The Secretary

Ministry of 
Social Transformation, 
Culture and Local Government
post of
COMMUNITY DEVELOP-
MENT OFFICER 1 
(lABORIE)
Qualifications :
Applicants should possess:
Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work, 
Community Development or Sociology, 
plus two (2) years experience in a post 
at Grade 10 and above 
or
Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work, Com-
munity Development or Sociology, plus 
eight (8) years total experience in a post 
at Grade 7 and above
or
Diploma in Social Work, Community 
Development or Sociology plus three (3) 
years experience in a post at Grade 10 
and above.
Computer literacy, experience in com-
munity work and ability to communi-
cate effectively in English and Patois 
especially at the group and community 
level would be an asset.
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to work under the direction of 
and report to the Assistant Director of 
Community Services and Local Gov-
ernment.  He/she will also respond to 
the Director of Community Services and 
Local Government on matters related to 
work in progress.  
The applicant will be required to:
mobilize, motivate and organize com-mu-
nities towards the development of com-
munity actions;
facilitate communities and Local 
Government Authorities in acquiring skills 
in needs assessment, resource identifi-
cation, project planning, implementation 
and evaluation;
facilitate the establishment and 
development of community groups and 
assist in providing the support services 
necessary for their effectiveness;
organize and facilitate the conduct 
of non-formal education/training pro-
grammes in keeping with the needs of 
the respective communities.
organize and promote community 
development projects and programmes 
in response to community needs;
promote self-help as a tool of com-munity 
development;
assist in the identification and develop-
ment of projects and programmes aimed 
at poverty alleviation/eradication;
ensure community awareness, prepared-
ness for disasters and mitigation plans;
assist communities in acquisition of 
requisite management skills for the 
management and maintenance of 
infra-structural facilities;
assist Council(s) in planning and im-
plementing work programmes and 
attend Council meetings as an ex-officio 
member;
document community development 
processes;
any other related duty as may be 
assigned from time to time by the 
Director and Assistant Director, Com-mu-

SAINT  LUCIA  GOVERNMENT  GAZETTE — MONDAY 16  FEBRUARY  2004  ISSUE 7
192
nity Services and Local Government.
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities:
The applicant should:
have the ability to demonstrate level of 
maturity to cope adequately with the 
varied problems and challenges 
encountered in the field;
have the ability to demonstrate leader-
ship qualities and the capacity to guide 
and facilitate the development of the 
geographical area assigned to him/her;
have a working knowledge of the 
historical and cultural background of the 
region to which assigned and St Lucia;
have the ability to maintain a quiet and 
cool composure, especially at stressful 
situations such as debates, arguments, 
confrontations etc.
Conditions:
The successful applicant will be 
required to:
work after normal working hours and 
during weekends whenever necessary;
function in a scheduled travelling post and 
therefore will be required to own, maintain 
and operate a motor vehicle  to facilitate 
effective discharge of duties;
travelling allowance will be paid in 
accordance with approved rates.
Salary:
Salary is in the range of $41,349.72 - 
$43,659.00 per annum (grade 12).
Applications on the prescribed form, 
along with Curriculum Vitae, certified 
copies of documents pertaining to quali-
fications and two (2) recent testimonials 
should be addressed to:
The Secretary
Public Service Commission
Block A, Waterfront
CASTRIES
to reach her no later than March 12, 2004.
Ministry of Physical Develop-
ment, Environment and Housing
post of
CIVIL  ENGINEER
Qualification:
Applicants should possess:
Level I
A Degree in Civil Engineering or 
Structural Engineering plus two (2) years 
working experience in a related field 
and Postgraduate qualifications in Civil 
Engineering or equivalent.
Level II
As for Level 1, plus four (4) years expe-
rience in a related field.
Level III
As for Level 1, plus four (5) years expe-
rience in a related field.
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to work under the direction of 
and report to the Chief Physical Planner 
and is required to respond whenever 
necessary to the Director of Planning on 
matters related to work in progress. He 
or she is expected to:
examine and advise on physical develop-
ment plans prepared in respect of water 
reticulation systems, drainage schemes, 
sewerage disposal plants and road net-
work engineering;
prepare plans for public water supply, 
solid waste  disposal. Public drainage, 
sewage disposal and flood control;
conduct research on environmental, 
structural and civil engineering issues;
review building construction plans in 
respect of structural and engineering 
details, surface and storm drainage, water 
supply and solid waste disposal;
examine land development plans in 
respect of drainage systems, road 
engineering, soil stability and other 
engineering aspects of land development;
advise the Section and Develop-
ment Control Authority (DCA)  on all 
engineering matters and provide repre-
sentation on all agencies and bodies in 
addition to co-ordination the engineering 
function of the section;
assess the adequacy of ongoing or com-
pleted road and drainage infrastructure 
works in land subdivisions relative to the 
Performance Bond requirements and 
other conditions of approval;
enforce the provisions of the Building 
Code and Guideline in development 
planning applications and in building 
construction and land development 
practice;
conduct Engineering Impact Assess-
ments of development projects and 
review and advise on the engineering 
component of Environmental Impact 
Statements;
undertake geo-technical studies, which 
may be required to determine land de-
velopment  issues resulting from devel-
opment planning applications;
present and defend engineering plans 
before in-house Committees or members 
of the DCA as required;
prepare an annual work programme and 
a quarterly progress report on the work 
programme for submission to the Chief 
Physical Planner;
perform such other duties as may be 
assigned from time to time by the Chief 
Physical Planner or Director of Planning.
Conditions:
The successful applicant will be 
required to function in a scheduled 
traveling post and will be required to 
maintain a motor vehicle for the prop-
er performance of duties. He/She will 
receive basic traveling allowance and 
mileage allowance in accordance with 
approved rates.
Salary: 
Salary is as follows:
Level I   (Grade 12)
$40,145.41- $42,387.40 (Grade 12) plus 
3% salary increase per annum
Level II   (Grade 14)
$48,763.01- $47,782.13 (Grade 12) plus 
3% salary increase per annum
Level III   (Grade 16)
$51,635.57- $53,527.21 (Grade 12) plus 
3% salary increase per annum
Applications on the prescribed forms 
along with references and certified 
copies of documents pertaining to qualifi-
cations, should be addressed to:
The Secretary,
Public Service Commission
Block A, Waterfront 
CASTRIES
to and reach no later than March 15, 
2004.
Please note that unsuitable applications

Ministry of Health, Human Services 
and Family Affairs
post of
FIELD NUTRITION OFFICER I
Qualification :
Applicants should possess: 
Diploma in Nutrition and Dietetics from a 
recognised institution
	
	
	
	
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to report and work under the 
direction of the Nutritionist.  He/she will 
also be required to respond whenever 
necessary to the Permanent Secretary 
or Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry 
of Health, Human Services and Family 
Affairs, on matters related to work in 
progress.
The applicant will be required to:
work in collaboration with the Nutri-
tionist to implement a nutrition 
education programme to improve the 
nutritional status of the community;
plan, develop, supervise, monitor 
and evaluate nutrition services in an 
assigned geographic area as part of the 
national nutrition programme;
co-ordinate within the geographic area, 
nutrition services with other operating 
programmes of the Ministry to which 
assigned and with related programmes 
of other Ministries;
participate in the preparation, review, 
selection and development of nutrition 
educational materials and techniques for 
dissemination of nutrition information to 
professional and non-professional audi-
ences through the mass media;
investigate food habits and conducts 
simple dietary surveys to determine 
eating practices of the community service 
and the cultural and socio-economic fac-
tors influencing these practices;
demonstrate methods of preparation 
of nutritious foods in clinics and/or 
community centres to groups within the 
assigned area;
lecture to students in nursing, public 
health inspection, other allied health 
workers and agricultural extension 
officers, as assigned;
provide nutrition consultation to 
physicians, nurses, social workers, 
teachers, agricultural extension officers, 
community development workers and 
other professional workers on current 
nutrition research finding and the practical 
application to personal community health;
make home visits to assist individu-
als or families with menu planning, 
food purchasing, food storage and 
food preparation skills, with a view to 
improving the nutritional value of their 
diets;
provide assistance to group feed-
ing programmes within the assigned 
community, advising on menus, food 
purchasing, preparation and storage 
methods and other food and nutrition-re-
lated aspects of the programme, e.g. 
Day Care Centres, “Meals-on-Wheels”, 
School Feeding Programmes, Resident 
Homes for children and the elderly;
report and summarize progress and activ-
ities at regular intervals, prepare periodic 
and special reports;
evaluate programmes in terms of objec-
tives and collaborates with Nutritionist in 
developing plans for the future.
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities:
The applicants should have:
knowledge of human nutrition in health 
disease;
knowledge of research methods and 
survey techniques used in assessment 
of nutritional status;
knowledge of principles of food service 
management;
knowledge of environmental and home 
conditions in community served by 
the Ministry and of the problems and 
attitudes of people residing there.  Ability 
to collect and maintain nutrition data;
ability to establish and maintain effective 
and harmonious working relations with 
individuals, families, community groups, 
Ministry of Health staff and staff of other 
relevant ministries;
ability to plan, interpret and promote the 
national food and nutrition programme.
Salary:
Salary is in the range of $22,875.84 - 
$25,401.60 per annum (Grade 6).
Applications on the prescribed form 
along with references and certified 
copies of documents pertaining to qualifi-
cations should be addressed to:
The Secretary
Public Service Commission
Block A, Waterfront
Castries
to reach her no later than March 15, 2004.
The Caribbean Centre 
for Development Administration 
(CARICAD)
post of
Deputy Director
Job Summary/Duties:
Management of the Programme 
Planning and Development, Central 
Administration, and Documentation 
Services Units.
Provision of administrative and man-age-
rial support to the Executive Director 
in implementing CARICAD’s strategic 
plan and raising the profile of and 
impact of the organization.
Coherent faclitation of operations and 
programmes consistent with CARICAD’s 
strategic direction.
Contributing to the building of stron-
ger relationships with donors, pro-fes-
sionals, governmental and non-
governmental organizations.
Exercise requisite control to ensure 
in-country PSR interventions are identi-
fied and implemented in accordance with 
the priorities and quality standards ac-
ceptable both to CARICAD and member 
countries.
Qualifications and Experience :
Post Graduate Degree in Public Man-
agement or related area, with at least 
10 years relevant working experience in-
cluding some level of exposure to project 
management.
Salary and Benefits: 
Comparable with qualifications and 
experience.

Caribbean  Development  Bank
post of
CONSULTANT  BUSINESS 
ANALYST
Information and Technology
Management Services Division
The appointment will be for a period of 
two years in the first instance.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Specifically, the Consultant Business 
Analyst will be required to:
Provide analytical support to all systems 
including the identification and articula-
tion of all system requirements and the 
implementation of automated systems 
developed making recommendations 
from time to time to users for their 
improved efficiency.
Provide project management and team 
leadership for the development of 
application systems ensuring that the 
activities are performed in accordance 
with the Systems Development Life 
Cycle (SDLC) methodology and within 
schedule.
Perform an interface function between us-
ers and the technical specialists maintain-
ing effective communication and ensuring 
mutual satisfaction and cooperation at all 
phases of the SDLC.
Participate in teams engaged in 
technology research and solutions 
development.
Qualifications and Experience:
Applicants should have a first degree 
in Computer Science or a related 
discipline with a minimum of five years 
experience interfacing with users, con-
ducting organisational reviews and 
process studies and documenting 
systems requirements utilising 
business process reengineering 
techniques; or
A Masters degree in Computer Science 
or a Masters in Business Administration 
with at least three years experience in 
organisational design and business pro-
cess analysis.
A working knowledge of client/server 
systems would be an asset.
Specific desirable skills for this position 
are as follows:
A comprehensive understanding of 
Systems Analysis Techniques.
A working knowledge of Project Manage-
ment Techniques.
A knowledge of Data Modelling 
Techniques.
An understanding of Database design 
with special emphasis on RDBMS.
A high level of writing, training and 
presentation skills.
Salary and Other Benefits:
Salary will be dependent on qualifications 
and experience. Life and medical  insur-
ances form part of the benefits package.
Applications:
Applications, including a detailed 
Curriculum Vitae, with details of age 
and nationality, as well as the names, 
designations, addresses and telephone 
numbers of three referees should be sub-
mitted no later than February 20, 2004 to:
The Deputy Director
Human Resource and Administration
Caribbean Development Bank
P.O. Box 408, Wildey
St. Michael
Barbados, West Indies
E-mail: recruit@caribank.org
Fax: (246) 427-4626
Information regarding CDB can be found 
at its website: www.caribank.org.

Ministry of Physical Development,

RECONNAISSANCE  SURVEY  OF 
CASTRIES  BASIN  COMMUNITIES
T
HE general public is hereby informed 
of the commencement of a 
Reconnaissance Survey of the many 
communities located within the Castries 
Basin, particularly those located in the 
upper levels of the catchment.
The purpose for this survey is to provide 
the Ministry of Physical Development, 
Environment & Housing with a better 
appreciation of the housing, land-use and 
related social issues and infrastructure in 
those communities.
Residents within the Castries Basin are 
therefore kindly requested to cooperate 
fully with the Ministry’s officials, who 
will be visiting your community and 
households, commencing 16 February 
2004. Ultimately, the main objective is to 
develop project proposals that seek to 
improve the quality of life for residents and 
the various communities in the Castries 
Basin.

SAINT LUCIA
	
DECLARATION OF ACQUISITION PURSUANT TO SECTION 3 OF THE LAND 
	
	
ACQUISITION ORDINANCE (CHAPTER 109)
And
	
IN THE MATTER of a Declaration by the Governor General acting on the advice of Cabinet 
that a certain portion of land situated at Gadette in the quarter of Dennery in the 
island of Saint Lucia is likely to be acquired for a public purpose.
DECLARATION  OF  ACQUISITION  OF  LAND
Whereas, it is enacted by Section 3 of the Land Acquisition Ordinance Chapter 109 that if the Governor General acting on the 
advice of Cabinet considers that any land should be acquired for a public purpose, she may cause a Declaration to that effect 
to be made;
And Whereas, it is considered by the Governor General acting on the advice of Cabinet that the land mentioned and described 
in the Schedule hereto should be acquired for a public purpose to wit: Gadette Public Health Facility.
Now Therefore, it is hereby declared by the Governor General acting in accordance with the advice of Cabinet, that upon the 
Second Publication of this Declaration in the Gazette, the land mentioned in the schedule hereto shall be acquired and vest 
absolutely in the Crown for a public purpose, to wit:- Gadette Public Health Facility.
SCHEDULE
All that piece of land being Part of Parcel 1641B 422 situated at Gadette in the quarter of Dennery belonging to Marie George 
aka Alice May Girard, Agnes Louis for Heirs of Joseph Pascal and Olivenia Virginie Pascal for Heirs Joseph Dominique Pascal 
and is bounded as follows:
	
North : By remainder of Parcel 1641B 422.
	
South : By remainder of Parcel 1641B 422.
	
East : By remainder of Parcel 1641B 422.
	
West: By Gadette/La Resource Road.
The whole is shown on plan of survey by Anthony Clarke, Staff Surveyor containing an area of 2,525 square feet dated June 11, 
1986 and lodged in the Survey Office on July 11th, 1986 as Plan No. D 1058B and recorded as 237/1986.
Dated this 4th day of February, 2004.
JAMES  FLETCHER, 
Secretary to the Cabinet.

Prime Minister discusses Bananas
P
rime Ministers Dr. Kenny Anthony of St. Lucia, and Dr. Ralph Gonzalves of St. Vincent and the Grenadines and Roosevelt 
Skerrit of Dominica travelled to London over the past weekend for a series of meetings aimed at promoting the interests of 
banana farmers in the Windward Islands.
Drs. Anthony and Gonzalves and Mr. Skerrit will hold talks with representatives of the main supermarket chains, which purchase 
Windward Island bananas including Sainsbury, Tesco, Waitrose and Marks and Spencers.
According to Dr. Anthony, the meetings are critical at this time as banana farmers in St. Lucia and the other Windward Islands 
have redoubled their efforts to increase production and improve on the quality of bananas shipped to the United Kingdom. The 
London visit will also lend support to the efforts by the Windward Islands Banana Exporting Company (WIBDECO), to intensify 
marketing of Windward Islands bananas in the United Kingdom. In addition to the meetings, Dr. Anthony and the Vincentian and 
Dominican Prime Ministers will visit banana reception depots and hold talks with Britain’s Minister of Agriculture, Lord Whitty. 
On Thursday February 12th at 7.30 p.m., the three Prime Ministers will address nationals of their respective countries in London 
and update them on developments at home and the importance of the banana industry to their economies.
On completion of their engagement in London, Dr. Anthony and Dr. Gonzalves will travel to Brussels for meetings with European 
Commissions responsible for Trade, Agriculture and Development. They will also meet with the president of the European Council. 
The St. Lucian Prime Minister is scheduled to return home on Saturday February 14th.
OECS Pressing Ahead with Family Law and Domestic Violence Initiative
S
aint Lucia and other OECS states are pressing ahead with the ongoing Family Law and Domestic Violence Reform 
Initiative. Manager of the Family Law and Domestic Violence Reform Project Marcia Lesmond, says currently, the focus of 
the project is to involve the public in the process, using a series of national and community consultations. 
According to Miss Lesmond, the consultations provide persons with opportunities to inform the policy frame work for the legislation 
and serve to generate feedback on the many social concerns, which will be addressed during the reform process. The green 
paper on Family law has highlighted several areas for reform, including the status of children, maintenance, unions other than 
marriage, and adoption.
To date, community consultations have taken place in Anse-La-Raye, Canaries, Soufriere, Dennery and Monchy.

The Regional Media to help Foster a Holistic Disaster Preparedness Culture
A
s a three-day CEDERA/CDB Hazard Mitigation and Planning workshop closed here on Thursday, February, 5th, 2004 work 
has commenced in earnest on the development of a more comprehensive approach towards disaster management. The new 
focus, being spearheaded by CEDERA under its Comprehensive Disaster Management (CDM) project, takes in account several 
activities of day to day living that require advance planning for disaster mitigation and reduction.
Information Manager at the Barbados headquartered CEDERA Terry Ally, said there was a dire need to move away from the re-
sponse and relief culture to a more holistic preparedness culture. That quest he noted would call for getting the entire population 
of a country on board in order to achieve success. “This in itself is a very mammoth task,” said Ally, quickly pointing out however 
that it was not impossible. 
To date a major initiative is underway aimed at heightening public awareness on this culture of preparedness though multi-media 
technology. That process is to be led by the various Government Information Services throughout the region. The hope is for the 
conceptualized of a campaign designed to bring the various publics from all member countries on board in order to foster that 
culture. 
Talks have already taken place with GIS representatives in Barbados, Grenada and St. Lucia with CEDERA due to hold dialogue 
with media representatives in Belize in the coming weeks.
The National Community Foundation to Garner Support for it’s Programmes of Assistance
S
ince it’s inception a little over a year ago the National Community 
	  Foundation (NCF) has spent over three hundred thousand dollars for its 
programmes of assistance.
Funding for the work of the NCF comes from chief benefactor the National 
Insurance Corporation, the Bank of St. Lucia, LUCELEC other corporate 
community and individual donors.
Last year the NCF introduced the telethon in an effort to augment financing 
of its programmes. As part of activities to mark the 25th Anniversary of Saint 
Lucia’s Independence, the NCF is for the second year, hosting the telethon 
to be held at the Pigeon Island Side Lawn on Sunday twenty-ninth February 
from one in the afternoon to seven in the evening. 
The foundation has distributed to it’s scholarship programme over two hundred thousand dollars, medical support in excess of 
ninety-two thousand dollars and funding for its elderly, homeless and youth at risk programmes totalling over thirty five thousand 
dollars.
Coordinator of the NCF Mrs. Relle Hippolyte says they are inundated with calls for help. She says they would like to assist ev-
eryone who comes to the foundation for support but she says invariably the demand outstrips the NCF’s capacity. The telethon 
she says is one of the foundations major activities to encourage donations from more than just the corporate community but all 
who would like to contribute both at home and away.
A co-sponsor of the telethon is Cable and Wireless. Again this year the company will be providing operators to man telephones, 
the internet lines to facilitate online contributions, and will work with the National Television Network NTN for a live webcast while 
NTN will broadcast live to St. Lucia.
This year’s telethon will feature a number of popular calypsonians including Gillo, Ashanti, the Mighty Mighty, the local cowboy 
Shervon Sealy and Star Quest winner Emrand Henry.
For further information contact Relle Hippolyte at (758) 453-6661.

The National Sports Awards Committee Introduces True Ambassadors 25
T
he Ministry of Youth and Sports is gearing up for the annual National Sports Awards.
This year the awards ceremony will take place on Friday February twentieth at the National Cultural Centre from 7:30 pm
Youth and Sports Officer Patrick Mathurin says there is a new addition to the programme which will enable the ministry to widen 
the pool of persons to be recognized.
Twenty five persons who have contributed to the development of sports at different levels as players, coaches and administrators 
will be honoured in the True Ambassadors 25 programme.
Mathurin says this segment was added especially as St. Lucia celebrates 25 years of independence.
The Youth and Sports Officers says at the close of nominations 35 names were received for the top awards of Sports Man and 
Woman of the Year, Junior Sportsman and woman Year and Association of the Year.
